headline: Figma's AI Agents Go Live Monday
subheadline: Figma's dropping a big release notes event on Monday about co-designing with AI agents — plus Cursor shipped parallel agents, Lovable went mobile, and Claude 5 is inching closer.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma's May 5 Event: Co-Designing with AI Agents
sections.description: Mark your calendar for Monday. Figma is doing a live release notes event focused on 'co-designing with AI agents' — live demos of real workflows from product teams using AI agents inside Figma. Given you're building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for your company's design system, this could directly impact your architecture decisions. New Make features include voice-to-text prompts, question cards, version history, and a Zapier connector.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Why Figma's MCP Update Is a Bigger Deal Than Any AI Demo
sections.description: This piece argues that Figma's MCP plumbing changes are more consequential than flashy AI demos — and you're literally building on top of this. Worth a read to see how others are framing the MCP shift, especially the 'how we'll build software' angle. Could validate or challenge your current integration approach.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Lovable Now Has a Mobile App — Voice-Code from Your Phone
sections.description: Lovable launched on iOS and Android this week, pitched as 'code on the go via voice.' Since you already use Lovable for vibe-coding, the mobile app could be interesting for those stroller-walk moments when an idea hits. Voice-prompt an app prototype while walking — that's a real use case for you right now.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Cursor's New Tiled Agent Layout: Run Multiple Agents in Parallel
sections.description: Cursor's May update adds a tiled layout for running multiple agents simultaneously, plus branch selection from empty state, diff-to-file navigation, and file search filters for tighter scoping. If you're doing any multi-file vibe-coding sessions in Cursor, the parallel agents view alone is a workflow upgrade worth exploring.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Agentic UX — When Products Become Execution Layers
sections.description: Two pieces this week converge on the same idea: AI agents are turning products from 'tools you operate' into 'execution layers that act on your behalf.' For a designer thinking about product leadership, this reframes what you're actually designing — not interfaces, but trust boundaries, delegation patterns, and fallback flows. The Phenomenon Studio article is the deeper read.

sections.label: Did you know
sections.title: Claude 5 Expected Q2–Q3 2026
sections.description: Anthropic hasn't confirmed the name, but the next major Claude release is projected for this quarter or next. Given your entire MCP + Claude integration workflow depends on Claude's capabilities, worth keeping an eye on — a model jump could meaningfully change what your Figma-to-code pipeline can do.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If AI agents can co-design in Figma, what does 'design leadership' become?
sections.description: Monday's Figma event is explicitly about teams co-designing with AI agents. You've led design teams. Soon you might lead teams where AI agents handle execution and humans handle judgment, taste, and strategy. What does a Group Head of Design actually do when the agents can push pixels? That might be exactly the role you're evolving toward.
